fixes.correction: Keep this composition. Nagoji is front right with the bamboo bier pole on his right shoulder, grey-haired elders bear the bier behind and beside him, and the young temple priest (ash marks, sacred thread, brass bell and smoking bowl) walks ahead on the right. Keep the wet courtyard with the jackfruit tree, the pyre stack and the walking stick against the trunk at right, and the open pale sky top centre for the caption. Fix Nagoji. Both his arms are entirely unmarked, with no scars, cuts, scratches, slashes or red marks anywhere on his skin. His free left arm hangs relaxed with the inner forearm turned in against his thigh, so the inside of that forearm never faces the camera. Gather his long curly hair into a firm Kerala topknot high on the crown, with only a few loose curls at the nape. Show a clear streak of grey at both temples, matching the close-up in the next panel. Keep his thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and tiny flush gold ear stud, and his plain borderless white mundu with the shoulder cloth knotted at the waist.
fixes.issues: v01 has the right staging: Nagoji at the front bearing the bier toward us, grey-haired elders, the shroud fully covering the body, and the V13 priest with ash marks and sacred thread walking ahead with his lips parted. But Nagoji fails the script and the bible. His hanging LEFT forearm faces the camera and shows three fresh-looking red diagonal slash marks. The script says the brand is turned away from camera, and the bible describes it as a pale puckered patch, so these read as new cuts or wounds. He also shows no grey at the temples, unlike panels 1.3 and 1.5, and his hair falls mostly loose to the shoulders around only a small crown knot, so it does not read as a Kerala topknot.

fixes.correction: Nagoji's RIGHT arm and hand must be completely unscarred: smooth skin on the right forearm and upper arm, with no scar lines, brand, scratches or marks. His LEFT forearm stays hidden behind Nandini or under the shoulder cloth. Show the guiding action exactly as written. Nandini grips the single iron stylus in her own small right hand, tongue caught between her teeth in concentration, and scratches her mark on the palm leaf. Nagoji's large right hand closes gently over her small hand to guide it. There is only one stylus, and no writing or letters are visible on any leaf. Keep everything else that worked: the verandah with the plain plaster wall at upper left left clear, the low dark-wood desk and brass lamp, and the tax collector waiting on the step at right with his palm-leaf bundle. Keep Nagoji's topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, white mundu with gold-bordered shoulder cloth and silver chain.
fixes.issues: v01 (only candidate): Nagoji's RIGHT forearm, the arm holding the stylus, carries a clearly visible curved pink scar across it, with scratch lines on the upper arm. The bible puts the brand and scar only on the inner LEFT forearm, and page 1 deliberately keeps that arm turned away. The script beat is also missing: Nandini does not hold a stylus or make her mark, and Nagoji is not guiding her hand. He writes alone while her hand rests flat on the leaf. Everything else works: verandah, plaster wall for captions, desk, brass lamp, tax collector with his palm-leaf bundle on the step, topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin, gold stud and silver chain.

fixes.correction: Tight insert of Marthanda Varma's right hand only (cream-and-gold cloth at the wrist edge, gold bangle, one gold ring), its index finger tracing the border of the small kingdom on the map. There are NO other people anywhere in the frame: no foreground shoulders or heads, no bearded man, no figure in red, no guards in the background, no faces at all. The map must be the same war-hall map as the previous wide panel. It is an unlabelled hand-drawn coast with territories shown only as flat ink washes and hatching: a large red wash to the north, black to the northeast, brown to the east, and tiny blue drawn hulls all along the sea. Travancore is a small, narrow green shape at the southern tip. The fingertip traces the edge of that green tip, which looks tiny against the big coloured washes pressing on it. There is no writing, lettering or symbol anywhere on the map. Behind the hand show only the soft-focus table edge and the laterite war-hall wall, with shuttered windows onto palm trees and no sea view, leaving plain wall at the top for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: v01 (only candidate): Two unscripted foreground figures appear. At top left is a bearded man with a gold hoop earring and a bare shoulder in white cloth, standing where Nagoji would be across the table, so he reads as a bearded Nagoji. At right is a figure in red cloth. Background guards show small faces, though the script asks for no face in frame. The map does not match 2.2: it has no red, black or brown territory washes, so the 'small against the inks pressing on it' beat is lost. The window looks out on the sea and a fort, unlike 2.2's palms. The hand itself (index finger tracing the coast, ring, gold bangle) is fine.

fixes.correction: Marthanda Varma himself makes the gesture. Standing as in the previous wide panel, he leans over the map from his side of the table and looks up across it at Nagoji, his own right hand open, palm down, passing over the map. Nagoji stands across the table, listening, with both hands visible and still at his sides or on the table edge, not gesturing. He carries no sword, knife or weapon and has no cravat: a plain standing coat collar, white European-cut coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain, as in the previous panel. Varma keeps his V13 face with pearl drop earrings, bare-headed with his hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, bare chest, gold necklaces, cream mundu with gold border. The map is the same unlabelled coloured map as before: a red wash north, black northeast, brown east, tiny blue hulls in the sea, and narrow green Travancore at the southern tip. There are no monograms, letter-like emblems or writing on any box, chest, banner or map. Keep the laterite war hall, brass lamps, spear rack and shuttered windows onto palms, with open wall and rafters above both heads for three balloons.
fixes.issues: v01 (only candidate): The action goes to the wrong person. Nagoji, standing, is the one whose open hand passes over the map, while Varma sits with his chin on his fist looking up. The scene now reads as an officer lecturing a seated king, though Varma is the one asking the question. Varma is seated here but stands in 2.2 and 2.5. Nagoji wears a brass-hilted sword and a white cravat that 2.2 does not show, and his left hand is hidden behind his back. Varma has no pearl earrings, unlike his V13 sheet and 2.2 and 2.5. A gilt motif on the chest at lower right looks like a monogram (pseudo-lettering). The map has lost 2.2's coloured territory washes. The room, lamps and Nagoji's face (stud, moustache, clean chin, grey temples) are fine.

fixes.correction: Make this a true close-up on Nagoji ALONE: head and shoulders filling the left two-thirds of the frame, three-quarter view, eyes lowered to the map. Keep his look from the current version (Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, white coat with brass buttons, red waistcoat, silver chain), but keep his hands away from his face so the CLEAN-SHAVEN chin is clearly visible. Marthanda Varma must NOT appear except as one hand and forearm entering from the right frame edge: cream cloth with a gold border at the wrist and a gold bead bracelet, the hand resting flat and still (not pointing) on a small hill town ringed in ink on the same beige, unlabelled map with drawn hulls as in panel 3.1. No other head, face, shoulder or torso anywhere in the frame. Ramayyan's stacked palm-leaf bundles sit soft and out of focus at the lower right edge. Same war hall, wooden pillars and warm lamplight as panel 3.1. Leave the upper third behind his head as a plain, dim laterite wall in soft shadow, with no windows or weapon racks, so two captions can sit there.
fixes.issues: Breaks the script beat: this is a two-shot, not a close on Nagoji. Marthanda Varma's full face and torso fill the right half, but the script says 'No other face in frame'. Varma is also drawn with Nagoji's grey temples, topknot and gold ear stud, so the two read as near-twins. Varma's hand points at the hill town with one finger when it should rest on it. Nagoji's fist covers his chin, so the clean-shaven chin cannot be checked in a close-up.

fixes.correction: Keep this exact composition, dusk palette and foreground: De Lannoy and Nagoji standing on the bund at the left, the felled palms across the road, the merchant cart turned back by Nair sentries in white mundu with spears, the supply carts with torches rolling along the bund, and the earth dam across the canal. Change the hilltop to the SAME old palace as panels 3.3 and 5.1: a Kerala palace of dark timber and laterite with steep, multi-tiered red-brown tiled gable roofs behind a laterite wall. It is fully INTACT, with no flames, no smoke and no fire on or among its buildings. Show the 'first siege fires' only as a ring of small orange campfires and watch-fires on the lower slopes and the plain around the foot of the hill, well below the palace. Remove every white flag and pennant from the poles; leave the poles bare or show no flags at all, so nothing reads as a surrender flag. Dress every figure at the carts in white, cream or earth-brown cloth, with no blue garments. Keep the open dusk sky above and to the right of the two officers' heads clear and low-detail for two speech balloons.
fixes.issues: The palace on the hill is a cluster of whitewashed, low-roofed buildings in a European or Goan villa style, unlike the steep-gabled Kerala palace in 3.3 and 5.1. Flames and smoke columns rise from the buildings themselves, so the palace reads as burning, but 5.1 shows it intact and the script wants only 'ringed by the first siege fires'. Plain white flags line the siege works and the bund. At a siege these read as surrender flags, and they undercut the single white truce cloth Nagoji's party carries in 5.1. A carter at the turned-back cart wears a blue tunic. Everything else works: De Lannoy (a head taller, pale hair with a black ribbon, plain white stand-collar coat) and Nagoji (topknot, grey temples, moustache, clean chin, ear stud, red waistcoat, silver chain) on the bank, the felled palms, the earth dam, the merchant cart turned back and the supply carts on the bund.

fixes.correction: Marthanda Varma's hair must be solid black with no grey anywhere: no grey streak and no grey at the temples, because only Nagoji is greying. Gather it into a neat side knot above his LEFT ear, not loose shoulder-length curls. Keep his V13 face, pearl drop earring, bare back, cream mundu with gold border, gold bead necklaces and his half-turn away from the table toward the shuttered window. The letter lowered at his side is one tightly rolled palm-leaf letter with a cut cord and a red lac seal split cleanly in two, not a loose bundle of strips. Keep Nagoji (topknot, first grey at the temples, clean chin, tiny gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat, silver chain, hands on the table), the war hall, the lamps, the map and the composition exactly as they are.
fixes.issues: Marthanda Varma has a clear grey streak at the temple and loose shoulder-length curls. The prompt's MUST MATCH says his hair is black, never grey, in a side knot above the LEFT ear. With grey temples and loose curly hair he reads as Nagoji's double: Nagoji stands across the map with the same grey temples, curls and moustache. In 4.1 Varma's hair is black and bound back, so this also breaks continuity on the page. The letter is also a loose bundle of strips, while 4.1 shows a rolled letter with a split red seal. Everything else is good: Nagoji matches his sheet and the bible (topknot, grey temples, clean chin, gold stud, uniform), Varma is turned toward the shuttered window, there is no text, and the upper wall has space for the balloons.

fixes.correction: Make Marthanda Varma in the foreground clearly distinct from Nagoji. Give him solid black hair with no grey at all (no streak at the temple), tied in a neat side knot above his LEFT ear rather than long loose curls. Use the pearl drop earring from his sheet, never a small gold stud, which belongs to Nagoji only. His cheeks and jaw are clean-shaven with no stubble shading. Nagoji's hands, wrists and forearms carry no tattoo, symbol or trident of any kind. His brand is a pale puckered patch on the INNER left forearm, kept turned from camera here; at most a faint white scar line may show. Keep the over-the-shoulder framing with Varma's hand-to-chin profile and eyes on nothing. Keep Nagoji level across the table with clasped hands, topknot, first grey at the temples, clean chin, tiny gold stud, white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain. Keep the lamps, the map with no writing and the war hall exactly as they are.
fixes.issues: Varma in the foreground is drawn as Nagoji's double. He has long loose curly hair with a grey temple streak, stubble shading, and a small gold ear stud, which is Nagoji's identity mark, in place of his pearl drop earring. The prompt says black hair, never grey, in a side knot above the LEFT ear. Two near-identical men face each other and a reader cannot tell them apart by face. Nagoji also has a crisp dark trident tattoo on the back of his left wrist. The bible has no tattoo or symbol: his only marks are the pale puckered brand and the white scar on the INNER left forearm. The over-the-shoulder composition, Nagoji's face and uniform, the room and the space for balloons are all good.

fixes.correction: Keep this composition, the pillared dark-wood hall, the lamplight and both figures as drawn (Nagoji standing still in his white coat, red waistcoat and silver chain, and Savitri in plain white walking around him and looking him up and down). Fix two errors. First, Nagoji must wear the same sheathed sword as in the previous panel: a brass-hilted sword in a dark scabbard hanging from his LEFT hip, its hilt clearly visible beside his left hand. Hold both his hands open and visibly a short distance away from that hilt, palms turned slightly outward, so he is plainly showing he will not draw. Second, Savitri wears no jewellery at all: no earrings, no ear studs, bare earlobes.
fixes.issues: The only candidate, v01, has no sword on Nagoji. He wears it in 5.1 and 5.2, and 6.1 has a retainer reach for it. The script beat is his hands held away from his sword hilt, so without a hilt the gesture means nothing. Savitri also has a small gold ear stud, but the script says no jewellery. Everything else works: the hall, the lighting, Nagoji's face (moustache, clean chin, ear stud), his costume, and Savitri walking around him looking up.

fixes.correction: Keep the composition, the hall, the brass lamps, the background retainers, and Nagoji's pose, face and uniform exactly as drawn. Fix Savitri's costume to match her sheet and the previous two panels. She wears a plain white short-sleeved blouse, its sleeves reaching mid upper arm, under the plain white neriyathu draped over her far shoulder, with no bare shoulder, no bare upper arm, no border and no jewellery. Change her expression to a cold smile with no warmth in it. Draw a thin, tight, closed-lip smile pulled to one corner of the mouth, with her eyes level, hard and slightly narrowed and looking straight into Nagoji's eyes. She must not gaze softly upward, and the smile must not read as kind, wistful or serene.
fixes.issues: The only candidate, v01, breaks Savitri's costume continuity. Her near shoulder and whole upper arm are bare, with the cloth over one shoulder only. Her sheet and panels 5.2 and 5.3 show a short-sleeved white blouse. Her smile is also wrong: it is soft and serene, with her eyes gazing gently upward, and reads as warm. The script asks for a smile with no warmth in it. Nagoji is correct (topknot, grey temples, thick moustache, clean chin, gold stud, uniform, level look), and the hall and lamps match the neighbouring panels.

fixes.correction: Savitri is a WOMAN of about fifty and must match the Savitri of Kottarakkara sheet exactly. Give her a woman's face with a smooth, bare upper lip: NO moustache, no facial hair, no upper-lip shadow, no stubble. Give her a softer feminine jaw, with lines of care only at the eyes and the corners of the mouth, and black hair streaked grey in a low knot at the nape. Make her white mundu and neriyathu visibly greyed with dust and smoke. Keep everything else exactly as composed: Savitri mounted on the dark brown horse at left-centre, reins in one hand, sword hilt at her side; her retainers in mundus with flintlocks and spears under the plain cloth banner with the dark palm-tree emblem and no script; the small roadside shrine in the palms at centre; the Travancore musketeers in white with crossed leather belts on the right; at the right edge, Nagoji's white-coated shoulder, red waistcoat collar, silver chain and the back of his dark topknot with grey at the temple and the gold ear stud. Keep the trampled paddy, the drifting smoke and the clear grey smoky sky across the top for the captions. No blood, no text.
fixes.issues: Savitri has a clear grey moustache and a masculine face. She reads as a man and does not match her sheet. Her white clothes are also clean, not grey with dust and smoke as the script asks. Everything else works: mounted on a dark horse with a sword hilt at her side; retainers in mundus with flintlocks and spears under a plain banner with a palm emblem; the roadside shrine in the palms; Travancore musketeers in white with cross-belts; Nagoji's white-coat shoulder, topknot and gold stud at the right edge; a smoky sky for the captions.

fixes.correction: Make this a TIGHT close-up across the field. Savitri's face and eyes fill the left-centre of the frame, framed from the shoulders up, matching her sheet: a woman of about fifty with a lean lined face, no facial hair, black hair streaked grey in a low knot, and dust on her plain white neriyathu. She is still MOUNTED on her dark brown horse as in the previous panel; show the top of the horse's mane and bridle just below her at the bottom edge. Her eyes are locked on the man in the right foreground. That man is NAGOJI, seen over the shoulder exactly as in the previous panel: the back and side of his head, with long curly black hair gathered in a Kerala topknot, grey at the temple, NO turban, NO beard, a small gold ear stud, the tip of his thick moustache, and a white European-cut coat shoulder over a red waistcoat collar and silver chain. No turbaned soldier in the foreground. Put drifting dust and grey smoke between them. Keep the same trampled paddy field, palms, roadside shrine and palm-tree banner soft in the background, and a clear grey smoky sky at the top for the caption. No blood, no text.
fixes.issues: This fails the beat and breaks continuity. (1) The over-the-shoulder figure Savitri glares at wears a white turban, has a beard and no ear stud, so he cannot be Nagoji (topknot, no turban, clean chin). The 'her eyes finding his' beat is lost. (2) She stands on foot among her men, but 7.3 shows her mounted. (3) The framing is a medium shot, not the tight shot the script asks for. Her face itself is good: a woman's lined face, grey-streaked hair, dust on her white clothes, no facial hair. The palm-tree banner, field, shrine and smoke match 7.3.

fixes.correction: The trodden banner in the foreground must carry the SAME emblem as the previous panels: a dark silhouette of a single coconut palm tree on a small mound, painted on plain cloth. It must NOT be a leaf shape, and nothing that could read as a cannabis leaf. The Dutch factors in dark civilian coats and tricorn hats must walk WEST, toward the setting sun: show them small in the distance, walking away from the viewer along the canal road toward the sunset and into the palms, not toward the right edge. No signature, monogram, scribble or marks of any kind anywhere in the image, especially in the bottom-right corner. Keep everything else as composed: the orange evening sky with the low sun, the emptied and trampled flooded paddy, spears standing in the mud, abandoned flintlocks and woven hats, the roadside shrine with its lamp in the palms at right, the canal. No bodies, no blood, no shore or sea. Keep the open sky across the upper left for the two captions.
fixes.issues: (1) The trodden banner's emblem is a seven-pointed leaf that reads as a cannabis leaf. It does not match the palm-tree emblem in 7.3 and 7.4. (2) Faint pseudo-text, like a signature, sits in the stubble at the bottom-right corner. (3) The sun sets at the left, but the Dutch factors walk to the right, so they head east, not west as the script says. Otherwise good: an evening paddy emptied of people, spears in the mud, abandoned flintlocks, the shrine in the palms, factors in dark coats on a canal road, no bodies, no blood, no sea, and an open sky for the captions.

fixes.correction: Savitri alone in the frame: remove the foreground over-the-shoulder figure at the right edge entirely (no bare-headed man in a white shirt with a maroon gold-bordered cloth). Keep everything else that worked: the tent interior with the open flap at sunset behind her, the two Nair guards with spears, the brass oil lamp and red bolster, and Savitri standing in plain white with the bruise on her right cheekbone. Keep her grey-streaked hair in a low knot, her wrists bound in front with coiled rough cord and her chin raised. If any listener shows at all, it may only be the out-of-focus edge of Marthanda Varma in the lower right corner: his cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest and a bare shoulder with gold pearl necklaces and cream-and-gold cloth. No other figure. Keep the upper tent canopy at top centre plain and low-detail for her speech balloon.
fixes.issues: An unscripted over-the-shoulder figure fills the right third of the frame. He is bare-headed with short dark hair and a moustache, in a white shirt with a maroon, gold-bordered cloth. He matches neither Varma (in 8.1: cream-and-gold turban with peacock crest, bare chest) nor Nagoji (topknot with grey temples, white European coat with brass buttons, red waistcoat). Readers will take him for the king Savitri is answering, so this breaks continuity. Savitri herself is good: bruise, grey-streaked low knot, bound wrists, chin up.

fixes.correction: Savitri's wrists must still be bound: two or three coils of rough brown cord around both wrists, tied together in front of her exactly as in the earlier panels of this page, with her joined hands resting in her lap and the cord clearly visible. Keep everything else as drawn: the full-width tent interior with the brass oil lamp at left and the open flap at sunset on the right with the guards outside seen from behind. Keep Savitri on the left in close profile facing right (plain white, grey-streaked hair in a low knot) and Marthanda Varma on the right in close profile facing her (cream-and-gold turban with jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare chest, gold pearl necklaces and armlet, cream-and-gold cloth). Nagoji stays out of frame. Keep her bruise on her RIGHT cheekbone, the side turned away from camera in this profile, at most a faint edge visible, never on the left cheek. Leave the plain tent cloth above both heads clear for two balloons.
fixes.issues: Savitri's hands are clasped in her lap with no cord on her wrists. The script calls for bound hands here, she is bound in 8.1 to 8.3, and page 9 (9.3, 9.4, 9.5) keeps her bound, so the binding vanishing breaks continuity and suggests she has been freed. Her bruise also sits on her left cheek, while the other panels show it on the right. Everything else is strong: the full-width tent, both in close profile facing each other, Varma in turban and crest, Nagoji absent, the guards outside, and clear tent cloth for both balloons.

fixes.correction: Draw Savitri alone in the frame. Do not draw any foreground or over-the-shoulder figure: no back of a head, no hair, no shoulder, cloth or garment entering from any frame edge. Marthanda Varma is off-panel to the right, and she leans forward toward the right edge as if facing him. Keep everything that worked in the previous attempt: the same campaign tent interior at sunset, the flap tied open on the field, Nair guards in white head cloths and white mundu with spears at the flap, the brass oil lamp, mats and red cushions. Keep Savitri seated and leaning forward with her rope-bound wrists held in front of her on her knees, the darkening bruise on her cheekbone, her grey-streaked hair in a low knot, the fierce scowl, and the same white clothes as the neighbouring panels. Keep the clear tent wall and sky in the upper part of the frame for three balloons.
fixes.issues: The script asks for Savitri alone, and v01 adds a large unrequested over-the-shoulder figure in the right foreground. It reads as the king she is addressing, but it has bare, loose, long curly black hair and no turban. In 9.1 and 9.4 Varma wears the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, so this breaks continuity between adjacent panels. It does not match Nagoji either: no topknot, no gold ear stud, and a gold-bordered drape instead of his white coat. Savitri herself is good: bruised cheekbone, grey-streaked low knot, bound wrists, leaning forward, fierce.
